title: The Last Ghost
premise: Coral Dunmore, a veteran interpreter for a doomed peace delegation in a fractured border state, receives calls on a burner phone from the voice of his dead mentor, Elias Vann — actually a living operative hidden inside the intelligence network that trained them both. The network, codenamed LANTERN, has been laundering war crimes as peacekeeping successes for two decades, and Vann wants Coral to help him expose it before an extraction flight at dawn carries the last witnesses out of reach. Betrayed by his own delegation, hunted through a city curfew, Coral must choose between the rules that kept him alive and the found family of translators and fixers LANTERN discarded. He burns the archive and broadcasts it himself, missing the flight on purpose, ending the story standing in the ash-dawn with nothing but the truth and the people who stayed.
about_author: Felix Thornbury is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent a decade interpreting in conflict zones before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about the people who carry other people's words across the lines of war.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. During ceasefire talks visibly collapsing in the capital, Coral finds a burner phone sewn into his old kit bag. It rings: Elias Vann's voice, dead for six years, asking if he remembers Sarajevo-adjacent village Krajina. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing; the past calling collect.

chapters.title: Rules of Interpretation
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback braided into present. We learn how LANTERN trained its interpreters to soften, omit, and reshape testimony — and how Coral obeyed for twenty years. Vann tells him the delegation he's interpreting for is itself a LANTERN production. Beat: vertigo; his whole career reframes as complicity.

chapters.title: The Delegation Eats Its Own
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He tests the phone's claims against the delegation's chief of staff, Mirela, and watches her stonewall with rehearsed precision. A junior translator, Denny, is detained after asking one question too many. Beat: first loyalty fracture; Coral chooses to investigate rather than report.

chapters.title: Krajina, Again
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Coral and Vann. Vann explains he faked his death when LANTERN marked him, and names the archive vault beneath the old radio station where twenty years of raw transcripts are stored. Beat: grief metabolized into purpose; the dead voice becomes a co-conspirator.

chapters.title: Curfew Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Martial law falls early. Coral recruits Denny, released and furious, and Mirela defects with a vault access code she was never supposed to keep. The trio forms an improvised family over stolen coffee. Beat: warmth kindling inside danger; found family assembled under curfew.

chapters.title: What the Transcripts Say
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Inside the vault antechamber they read a single file: a massacre Coral personally interpreted into something gentler. Mirela reveals her brother is on those tapes. Beat: shame made physical; Coral confesses his role aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: The Extraction Flight
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. LANTERN discovers the breach; the dawn flight will now carry not witnesses but the network's leadership and sanitized records. Vann offers Coral seats on it — safety, exile, silence. Beat: temptation sharpened into betrayal; the easy exit priced in complicity.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The plan: copy the archive, torch the vault, uplink everything to every newsroom before the plane wheels lift. Denny takes the antenna roof, Mirela the power junction, Coral the server room — where he finds Vann waiting, held there by LANTERN handlers. Beat: clock-tight terror; every ally exposed.

chapters.title: Dawn, Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. Coral fights the handlers while the upload crawls; Vann takes a bullet meant for him and dies for real this time, telling Coral to let the plane go. The files land worldwide as the jet lifts off half-empty, its passengers already named. Beat: sacrifice transmuted into justice outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Last Ghost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, weeks later. Testimonies reopen; Coral testifies in his own imperfect voice, no longer translating anyone. He keeps the burner phone, silent now, and visits Denny and Mirela in a city learning its true history. Beat: quiet reckoning; memory kept honest at last.
